record.original_question: Let G be a graph homeomorphic to the Petersen graph. If each path in G made of two successive segments is a geodesic, each cycle of G containing five segments has odd length, and all cycles of G containing six segments have equal length, are these three conditions not only sufficient but also necessary for G to be geodetic?

evidence.quote: It is known that the following three conditions are sufficient for a homeomorphic graph G to the Petersen graph to be geodetic:
(1) Each path composed of two successive segments, one followed by the other, is a geodesic in G.
(2) Each cycle of G containing five segments has odd length.
(3) All cycles of G containing six segments have equal length.
It is conjectured that the three conditions of each of the two previous statements are not only sufficient, but also necessary [6].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ denote the Petersen graph, and let $G$ be a graph homeomorphic to $P$; that is, $G$ is obtained from $P$ by subdividing each edge of $P$ a (possibly zero) number of times. Call the images in $G$ of the original edges of $P$ the segments of $G$. A graph $G$ is called geodetic if between every pair of vertices of $G$ there is a unique shortest path. Consider the following three conditions on $G$:

(1) Every path in $G$ formed by two consecutive segments is a geodesic of $G$.
(2) Every cycle of $G$ that consists of exactly five segments has odd length.
(3) All cycles of $G$ that consist of exactly six segments have the same length.

It is known that conditions (1), (2), and (3) together are sufficient for $G$ to be geodetic. Determine whether these three conditions are also necessary: that is, prove or disprove that every geodetic graph $G$ homeomorphic to the Petersen graph must satisfy (1), (2), and (3).
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that the characterization of geodetic graphs homeomorphic to the Petersen graph is an active topic, with the three conditions established as sufficient. No clear published resolution of the necessity direction (the "Petersen necessity conjecture") was found, and the broader characterization problem for geodetic subdivisions is described as still open.

status_evidence.title: Geodetic Graphs Homeomorphic to a Given Geodetic Graph
status_evidence.snippet: Describes sufficient conditions for a graph homeomorphic to the Petersen graph to be geodetic, and approaches to characterizing all such graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The three conditions are known to be sufficient; necessity is not established in the located sources.

status_evidence.title: Topological Analysis and Synthesis of Structures related to Petersen graph
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses subdivisions of the Petersen graph and the open problem of characterizing geodetic subdivisions.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of geodetic subdivisions of the Petersen graph remains an open area of investigation.
